facts.text: Watson was incorporated December 2, 1907, but its roots trace back to a railroad station built in 1868 that briefly served as Desha County’s seat from 1874 to 1880.
Every year since 1960, Watson hosts the Watson Fish Fry, an event that draws over 1,000 visitors and raises money for local projects through auctions.
French trappers and the Quapaw first settled the area that became Watson along ancient river routes, with early European influence from Arkansas Post founded in 1686.
Watson’s early economy relied on cotton and corn plantation agriculture on the fertile alluvial soils of the Mississippi floodplain, a legacy that still shapes the region’s farming today.
